title: Look up token embeddings
statement:
Step 2 · Represent text

An embedding table has one learned row per token. Looking up IDs produces a sequence-by-width matrix. Repeated IDs share parameter values, but this exercise returns independent row copies.

Build it

Return one copied embedding row per token, preserving token order. IDs are valid table indices; all rows have the same width.

Contract: Implement embed using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: tokens = [0, 2, 0], table = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [0.5, 0.5]]
Expected: [[1, 0], [0.5, 0.5], [1, 0]]
Input: tokens = [], table = [[1, 2]]
Expected: []
Hint

Index a row for each ID, then copy it rather than returning an alias.

Review your understanding

What are the shapes for a sequence of 128 tokens and an embedding width of 64?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
